title: Join on Multiple Columns (Composite Key)
description: Reconcile **shipments** with **order line items** by joining on both `order_id` AND `product_id` (a composite key). For each matched pair, show the ordered quantity vs shipped quantity and compute the difference.
solution_sql: SELECT s.order_id, s.product_id, oi.price, oi.quantity AS ordered_qty, s.quantity AS shipped_qty, s.quantity - oi.quantity AS qty_difference FROM shipments s JOIN order_items oi ON s.order_id = oi.order_id AND s.product_id = oi.product_id ORDER BY s.order_id, s.product_id

test_cases.description: 8 order-product pairs. Order 103/product 2: ordered=4, shipped=3 (difference=-1). All others match exactly.

hints: A composite key join uses AND in the ON clause: JOIN ... ON s.order_id = oi.order_id AND s.product_id = oi.product_id — both columns must match.
Joining on only one column (e.g., just order_id) would produce incorrect cross-matches between different products in the same order.
explanation: Composite key joins are essential when no single column uniquely identifies a row in the join context. Here, order_id alone isn't unique within order_items (one order has multiple products). The AND condition ensures each shipment row matches exactly the correct product within its order. Order 103, product 2 has a discrepancy: 4 ordered vs 3 shipped (difference=-1). All other 7 pairs match perfectly (difference=0).
